name: CA-36
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+21 district partisanship in a deep-blue Los Angeles-area seat
Incumbent Ted Lieu running with a large financial advantage
Republican opponent raised only about $5,000 with no outside support
Prediction markets price Lieu near 95% to win
model.rationale: The fundamentals point overwhelmingly to Lieu: a D+21 seat, a well-funded incumbent, and a challenger who has raised barely any money. Markets price this as a near-certain Democratic hold, and nothing in the evidence suggests meaningful risk.
model.watch: Any late surge in challenger fundraising or outside spending would be the only realistic sign of movement, though it would need to be extraordinary to matter.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Ted Lieu seeks another term in a Los Angeles-area district that leans Democratic by about 21 points. He enters the general election with roughly $1.2 million on hand, while Republican Houston Brignano has raised about $5,000 and reports under $1,000 in cash. No outside groups are spending against Lieu, and prediction markets give him roughly a 95 percent chance of winning.

No public polls cover the race, so the forecast rests on district partisanship, incumbency, and the lopsided money gap. All signs point to a comfortable Democratic hold, with the only uncertainty being the exact size of the margin rather than the outcome.
